incident-bot: Alert: Elevated error rate detected for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (5xx spike). Pager routed to on-call. Monitoring: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/1937654321

Sam O'Neill (on-call): Got it, paging in. Seeing timeouts on the GPU pool. Investigating.

Maria Chen (IC): I'm taking incident command. Sam, quick status? impact to customers and any rollbacks started? :eyes:

Sam O'Neill (on-call): No rollbacks yet. Error rate ~18% on requests to the hosted generation endpoint, latency up to 2.1s p95. Affected region us-west-2 only. No dedicated customers reported via support yet.

Maria Chen (IC): Alex can you draft a short initial status update for status page + customer comms? Keep it conservative, mention we're investigating.

Alex Ruiz (comms): Draft incoming. Will keep it minimal: initial message, what we know, scope, mitigation in progress, next update ETA 30m. Posting below for quick review.

Alex Ruiz (comms): ```Initial update (draft):
We are investigating increased error rates for the Redwood Hosted Text Generation API in the US-West (us-west-2) region. Some requests to /v1/generate may return errors or experience elevated latency.

Impact: Potentially affects a subset of customers using the hosted generation endpoint in us-west-2.

What we are doing: Our on-call engineering team is actively investigating and working to restore normal service. We'll provide updates as we have more information.```

Jordan Park (SRE): Suggest adding whether data loss is expected (no) and an estimated user-facing risk. Also maybe include a rolling mitigation: diverting traffic to other regions is possible but needs approval.

Alex Ruiz (comms): Updated draft with Jordan's notes. ```Update v2 (draft):
We are investigating increased error rates for the Redwood Hosted Text Generation API in the US-West (us-west-2) region. Some requests to /v1/generate may return errors or experience elevated latency.

Impact: A subset of customers using hosted generation in us-west-2 may experience errors or slower responses. We have no indication of data loss or compromise at this time.

What we are doing: On-call engineers are actively investigating. We are evaluating routing options to reduce customer impact and will implement mitigations where safe. Next update: ~30 minutes.```

Priya Patel (support): FYI, we have three tickets mentioning timeouts from EU customers hitting the us-west region via APIGW fallback. They're being triaged.

Jen Walters (legal): Please avoid speculative timings or guarantees. The phrasing looks fine. Also don't mention internal tools or specifics (e.g., GPU pools) in the public message.

Alex Ruiz (comms): Noted, removed infra details. Final public draft below for publish approval: ```Public update (candidate):
We are currently investigating increased errors and elevated latency for the Redwood Hosted Text Generation API in the US-West (us-west-2) region. Some requests to /v1/generate may fail or be slower than normal.

Impact: A subset of customers using hosted generation in the US-West region may be affected. We have no indication of data loss or compromise at this time.

What we are doing: Our engineering team is actively investigating and evaluating routing and recovery options. We will post another update within ~30 minutes or as the situation changes.```

Maria Chen (IC): Approve to publish to status page and send an email to customers flagged as active in us-west? Alex, can you coordinate with support on an email?

Alex Ruiz (comms): Publishing status page now, and looping in Priya for the customer email. 

deploy-bot: statuspage: Creating incident post... https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/ir-1937654321 (draft)

Alex Ruiz (comms): Published initial update to status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/ir-1937654321 :white_check_mark:

Priya Patel (support): I'll send a short targeted email to the ~12 customers flagged as active in us-west. Email template: ```We are investigating increased errors and latency for the Redwood Hosted Text Generation API in US-West. Our team is actively working on mitigation. We'll update you within 30 minutes. If you are seeing production impact, reply to this thread.```

Sam O'Neill (on-call): Update from investigation: root cause appears to be a memory leak in a model-worker process causing restarts and transient 5xx. Restarting affected pool nodes seems to reduce error rate. Continuing remediation.

Jordan Park (SRE): Rolling restarts started on the affected GPU pool at 1937654700. Monitoring error rate.

Alex Ruiz (comms): Drafting first follow-up update (30m): ```Follow-up update: Our engineers identified an issue causing increased errors in the US-West region and have started remedial restarts of affected worker processes. Error rates are decreasing but some residual errors may still occur. We will continue to monitor and provide another update in 20 minutes.```

Maria Chen (IC): +1 to send. Jen, any legal concerns with follow-up wording?

Jen Walters (legal): Still good. Avoid specifics like exact host counts. The current wording is fine.

Alex Ruiz (comms): Follow-up posted to status page and sent in the incident channel. https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/ir-1937654321/updates/2

Sam O'Neill (on-call): Error rate now ~1.8%. p95 latency ~450ms. Some requests still hit hiccups but much improved.

Priya Patel (support): Getting fewer customer reports. I'll update the ticket queue and inform customers we've posted a fix in progress.

Jordan Park (SRE): Monitoring shows stabilization across us-west after completions of restarts. No further restarts planned.

Maria Chen (IC): Let's prepare a resolution message but hold until we have stability for 15m. If stable, publish resolved with root cause and postmortem ETA.

(15 minutes later)

Sam O'Neill (on-call): Stabilized at 0.1% errors for last 15m. All checks green.

Alex Ruiz (comms): Drafting resolved notice: ```Resolved: We have restored normal service for the Redwood Hosted Text Generation API in US-West (us-west-2). The issue was caused by a memory leak in a model worker process which led to elevated restarts and transient 5xx responses. Engineers performed rolling restarts to restore capacity. Impact: A subset of customers experienced intermittent errors and elevated latency between 2026-03-15T02:45Z and 2026-03-15T03:20Z. There is no indication of data loss or compromise. A post-incident report will be published within 72 hours. Thank you for your patience.```

Jen Walters (legal): Timelines look plausible. Avoid naming internal component "model worker" in public message — use "internal worker process".

Alex Ruiz (comms): Updated resolved draft and publishing now.
